Question
========
Which of the following statements about XML element names are correct?

Answerlist
----------
* Element names are case sensitive, so `<Bike>` and `<bike>` count as two different elements.
* An element name is allowed to start with a digit, for example `<1bike>`.
* An element name may not start with the letters "xml", in any combination of upper and lower case.
* Element names are allowed to contain spaces, as long as the name is written in quotes.
* The same element name can appear more than once within one document.


Solution
========
Element names in XML are case sensitive, which means `<Bike>` and `<bike>` are treated as entirely different elements - mixing them up is a common source of "invalid document" errors. A name must start with a letter or an underscore, never with a digit, and it may not begin with any variant of "xml" (such as XML, Xml, xML), since that prefix is reserved. Spaces are never allowed inside element names, regardless of quoting - quotes are used for attribute values, not for element names. There is nothing stopping the same element name from being reused at different points in the document, for example several `<bike>` elements inside one `<location>` element.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* False
* True
* False
* True
